parsed.basis: Djibouti has no express offence criminalising consensual same-sex conduct, but penal provisions on good morals and public morality are described as treating such conduct as de facto illegal, with no case law bounding their application to a visibly transgender visitor. There is no legal gender recognition procedure and no general anti-discrimination protection for service, housing or facilities, with recourse limited to police complaints or the national human rights commission. Official violence is not cited, while social and religious intolerance is described as pervasive and disclosure taboo. Documentation is thin, and no region-specific information distinguishes Tadjourah from the national picture.
